en: Aniki. I got this tubby chump.
Go on ahead with Tagashira.

Hey, dumbass. I dunno if
the main family sent ya or not...

...But I'm captain o' the Hirose Family.
Don't y'dare underestimate me.

If y'wanna try me on for size,
y'better be ready t'pay the price!
Let's goooo!
So we should head up?

Yeah. Cap's buyin' us some time,
so let's hurry.

Looks like we're in some kinda
old shipbuildin' station.

This is where the code was takin' us.
Let's get down there!

Crap! 
We've got a welcoming party...

They really want to keep this
secret safe, don't they?

That's fine.
Try to stop me if you can.
Your numbers don't impress me.

You want to see what a yakuza really is?
I'll show you.
Come on!

Commissioned during the war, but never completed...
Abandoned in planning, according to the history books.

In truth, Iwami Shipbuilding continued construction
under highly confidential military orders.

But thanks to the war,
our workforce was nonexistent.

So we approached the Saio Triad, to recruit poor
Chinese refugees looking for an escape.

That is the only reason the Saio leader
had any knowledge of the secret of Onomichi.
Lo said he learned of it from his father.

Regrettably, the ship was still in its final
stages of
 construction as the war ended.

Iwami Shipbuilding faced immeasurable losses.
Then, a man came forth to shoulder the burden.
And that was?

A high-ranking naval officer by
the name of Minoru Daidoji.

Minoru Daidoji?
That name sounds familiar...

Daidoji felt the Yamato Mark II a necessary risk for the
survival of Japan, and unilaterally funneled funds to us.

It was essentially an embezzlement of war funds.
His career would be over if it came to light.

As such, when the occupying forces ordered our country's
demilitarization, we opted instead to hide the battleship.

And in exchange for keeping this blight
confidential, Daidoji promised me compensation.
Compensation?

I remember now! Daidoji's the guy all those
people on the news're callin' the Fixer!
They were sayin' he's in critical condition!

Indeed. Occupying forces
 withdrew
from our shores in 1952.

Free from the gaze of the American army, Daidoji
gained influence over the post-war administration.

Those connections allowed him unauthorized access
to the funds
 used to repay Iwami Shipbuilding.

Beyond that, he continued to compensate me
by
 pushing bills through that benefited my ventures.

It was a gross misappropriation
of our nation's legal system.

Alongside Daidoji, I came in contact with
a variety
 of underhanded government workers.

Our cooperation laid down a complex
 network of roots
beneath our nation's political facade.
These roots still impact politics as we know them today.

The Yamato Mark II was the only physical proof
of my countless years of governmental collusion.

To Daidoji and the administration, it was a secret
they could nigh afford to have made public.

Even the Yomei Alliance was created
as a means of ensuring it stayed hidden.

Upon its founding, the Yomei Alliance consisted of
Iwami managers who had helped build the ship.

Each one had to be carefully monitored
to ensure they were following protocol.
Keeping the secret safe was our sole purpose.

That is why we were content with independence.
We had no need to expand beyond Hiroshima.
One day though, 30 years after the war...

Daidoji approached me and forced me to promise
that the secret would stay hidden for all of eternity.

At the time, those who knew the secret of Onomichi
were dwindling and getting on in years.
I decided it best to kill them all.
You did what...?

That's when I commanded Hirose to murder
every last one of our Yomei Alliance brethren.
He was the strongest man in Hiroshima, after all.

Patriarch Hirose.
Why would you ever agree to that?

Even if your boss gave the order...
You didn't have to agree.

I doubt you'll understand this...
but I'll give it a shot.

It was after the bomb turned Hiroshima into
a charred wasteland. I'd just started a little street gang.
I was only 14 at the time.

One day, one of my guys had a strange idea. He wanted
to
 break into Iwami Shipbuilding. Steal from them.

I wasn't that interested...
But I was the leader. I had to act tough.
Couldn't say no, really.
So, the next day, we busted in. But...

I have to wonder, what kind of excuse
were you planning to give Daidoji?

As you know, keeping the Yamato Mark II
under wraps was your job. Your responsibility.

However, it seems you were
unable to fulfill that duty.

No matter what you say now,
Daidoji would have no reason to listen to you.
I don't know what you're talking about.
I suppose I've never mentioned this before<symbol=em_dash_with_outline>

But I've known the secret of
Onomichi this whole time.

Whenever I spoke to you,
I merely feigned ignorance.

It was 40 years ago. When I was just a kid,
a Yomei officer named Matsunaga came to me.
He rattled off every last detail.

At the time, those with knowledge of the secret
were being slaughtered one by one.
Matsunaga feared he was next.

So, he chose to entrust me with the secret.
He also asked that I beg you to spare his life.
Tragically, Matsunaga died that very evening.

But I must say, you botched your own plan.
You should have silenced everyone at once.

Now then, Daidoji and his sympathizers gave you
a great deal to keep their battleship hidden.
Political favors of that magnitude are no light matter.
Most would consider that to be governmental collusion.
What are you getting at?

Over the past 70 years, countless politicians and diplomats
have involved themselves in your plot with Daidoji.

If that were to come out, our society's darkest secrets
would be dragged into the light in rapid succession.

To prevent that, they want to
ensure your eternal silence.

And that, is where I come in.
I am the contractor who can fulfill their desire.
I only have one more question for you.

Father... Why did you keep
the secret of Onomichi hidden even from me?

What did you stand to gain from
leaving your own son in the dark!?

If you had known the truth, you would
have been doomed to a life of crime.

That is not the path I wanted
my child to walk in the world.
No parent would.

Interesting. So that's why you chose
to have me inherit Iwami Shipbuilding.

Yes. It's a world-class shipbuilding manufacturer.
You should have been pleased.

That's nothing more than your own selfish opinion!
Whether or not I'm pleased... is my choice.
What else could you want?
You know, I waited for so many years.

Not just to take over your front, but to be
accepted into your criminal organization as well.
I didn't want to use the secret of Onomichi as a crutch.

All I wanted was for you to
recognize the potential I had!
I should have realized you had no intention of that.
So I took matters into my own hands.

I made a fool of the Saio Triad's Lo. Won over Sugai.
Turned the Tojo Clan into mere pawns in my hand.

Those are achievements worthy of
the next chairman of the Yomei Alliance.
You have done much.

But because you brought Lo here behind my back,
the battleship's existence was exposed.

You say that, but remember the oath I
attempted to barter with the Tojo Clan?
The one you asked Kazuma Kiryu to witness?

In truth... You only chose him because
you knew full well that he would decline.
It was all part of your plan to rein me in, yes?

However, had you allowed the oath to proceed,
we would have gained free rein over Kamurocho.

In fact, the secret would still be under wraps as well.
Lo would have been taken care of long ago.

So according to you, I am at fault for allowing
the Yamato Mark II to become known to the world.
Exactly. And Daidoji sees it my way.

I must say, it was quite a surprise to see
that ship surfacing on the horizon.

However, it has given me a perfect opportunity.
The time is nigh for me to take my rightful role.
Hey. You should try to eat, Nagumo-kun.

It ain't gonna happen, Kiyo-chan.
I ain't hungry...

What about Moreno, Boss?
Y'sure it's okay to be closed today?

Yeah. Actually, let's take tomorrow
n' the next day off, too.
Junko. I'll take a rice ball.

Last night, a massive battleship surfaced in the Iwami
shipyard, Onomichi, measuring in excess of 300 meters.

It is thought to be even bigger than
the previous world record holder, the Yamato.

The management at Iwami Shipbuilding claims they do not
know when or how this ship could have been constructed.
An internal investigation has been opened.

When there are any findings to announce, a press
conference has been promised that we will carry.
The company remains in turmoil.
I just heard from Yuta.

He said Haruka's regained consciousness.
Apparently, she can even talk a bit, too.
F-Fer real?

What a relief.
Man, I'm glad t'hear that.
Kiryu-san... That's great news.
Sorry for bringing it up now.

What're y'talkin' about?
Y'don't gotta apologize fer that.
I dunno, Aniki.

Right now, I ain't really sure
how I'm s'posed t'be feelin'.

I jus' can't get my mind off what the boss
was sayin' right before he died.

Y'know, that part about how he wished
we coulda been the ones who killed him.

It's weird, though. Even though he told
me he was the one who murdered my dad...

...I probly never woulda wanted
t'get revenge on him.

I jus' don't get it. Why can't I bring myself
t'hate him fer killing my dad?
It's mutual, Cap.
I was still in elementary school when my dad died.
I barely even remember that day at this point.

Only thing that comes t'mind when
I think of my dad... is Hirose-san's face.

We were all alone in the world,
but the boss came n' took us in.

I was so happy swearin' my oath t'him. That was the day
I could finally start thinkin' o' him as my dad fer real.

If one thing's clear to me, it's that the bond
between you and your boss was very strong.

At first I'm sure the guilt ate away at him,
so he took you guys in as a way of repenting.

But... the more time you spent together,
the more he grew to love you like his own children.

If that wasn't the case, he would've done as Kurusu
asked. You would have died back at the shipyard.

To me, it looks like you guys helped release
your boss from the curse that hung over him.
Cap... Matsunaga-aniki...

In that case... It's okay fer us t'cry
over losin' our boss, right?
It's Kiryu.

I happen to be in the area.
Can you meet, Fourth Chairman?
Is this... Someya?

Yes. I have something I'd like to tell you.
I'll wait for you at the docks.

So that's the secret of Onomichi...
It's breathtaking.
You came alone?

Yes. That should be plain to see,
Fourth Chairman.
And what do you want?

First, please accept my condolences.
I heard of Hirose-san's passing.
It is a difficult time for Onomichi.

You may not be aware, but
Takeru Kurusu died last night as well.
It was suicide, apparently.

Well... the only one actually saying
it was suicide is Tsuneo Iwami.

Wait, so Tsuneo Iwami... killed his own father?
Just what exactly is going on here?

Didn't I say I had something to tell you?
Calm down and I'll explain everything.

So Tsuneo knew, too.
He was in on the secret of Onomichi.
He's known for the past 40 years.

Beyond that, his silencing of Takeru Kurusu last night
authorized him to inherit the Yomei Alliance throne.
It appears we underestimated him.
Tsuneo Iwami is a yakuza through and through.

I'd planned to seize control of the Tojo Clan
from Sugai while the sixth chairman was gone.

However, if Sugai has Iwami's support,
it won't be as easy as I had expected.

And why come to me with all this?
What's your goal here?
I doubt you'll be able to trust me...

...But quite frankly, I'd rather not see you
murdered by the likes of Tsuneo and Sugai.

It appears Daidoji has instructed them
to dispose of you, Fourth Chairman.

You exposed the secret of Onomichi, after all.
Daidoji will never forgive you for that.

Being inches away from death's door,
he has discarded all false pretenses.

As such, he will be coming for both
you and the Hirose Family.

As long as you stay in town, the Yomei Alliance
will continue sending soldiers to kill you.
Every last yakuza in Hiroshima is here.

I'm fairly convinced even a man like you
can be overwhelmed, Fourth Chairman.

Not that I see you actually dying before
such weak foes.

I should also make it clear that I'm only here now
because Sugai ordered me to kill you myself.

To be blunt, Sugai intends to sell
the entire Tojo Clan to Tsuneo Iwami.
